title: Fully faithful simplicial descent for algebroids
statement: Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal, and use [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $C_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ be a small coherent simplicial diagram such that every structure map $C_m\to C_n$ is fully faithful. Put $X_n=U(C_n)$, where $U$ is object space. Its geometric realization $C=|C_\bullet|$ satisfies $U(C)\simeq|X_\bullet|$, compatibly with all cocone maps. For every $n$ and $x,y\in X_n$, the cocone induces an equivalence $C_n(x,y)\to C(\bar x,\bar y)$ of objects of $\mathcal V$. Thus every cocone map $C_n\to C$ is fully faithful. No essential-surjectivity assumption on the structure maps is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, proof paragraph on the Segal-presheaf model and its cartesian squares (generalized to arbitrary fully faithful simplicial diagrams); Theorem 4.5.3; HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9 (read online; not archived in literature/). No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model], choose a small monoidal infinity category $B$ and a monoidally compatible small set $S$ with $\mathcal V\simeq P^S(B)$. Use its natural equivalence $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)\simeq Q_B^S\subset P(B_\otimes)$ to represent the given coherent diagram by $F_\bullet$. The inclusions here are full subcategories. Under this equivalence $F_n([0])=X_n$, and the mapping presheaf $H_{F_n}(x,y)$ represents $C_n(x,y)$ in the full subcategory $P^S(B)\subset P(B)$. It is $S$-local. In the rest of the proof all limits, fibers and products of spaces are homotopy limits, fibers and products. The indexing category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the label category $B_\otimes$ are small, in the universe convention of [def-coef-complete-algebroid].

source.place: Definition 4.3, Proposition 5.1, Proposition 8.2 and Observation 8.4; use the fiberwise localization characterization of the cited DAG model, rather than the uncorrected wording of Proposition 8.5

proof.text: Fix a label $q=[r](b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ and a structure arrow $m\to n$ of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Consider the endpoint square with top row $F_m(q)\to F_n(q)$ and bottom row $X_m^{r+1}\to X_n^{r+1}$. Over a tuple $(x_0,\ldots,x_r)\in X_m^{r+1}$, the Segal condition identifies the homotopy fiber of its top-left corner over the bottom-left corner with $\prod_{i=1}^r H_{F_m}(x_{i-1},x_i)(b_i)$; the analogous fiber of the pullback of the top-right corner is $\prod_{i=1}^r H_{F_n}(f x_{i-1},f x_i)(b_i)$. Full faithfulness of $C_m\to C_n$ makes each factor map an equivalence, by the mapping-object identification in [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model]. Thus the pullback comparison is an equivalence on every homotopy fiber. Apply the fiberwise comparison criterion of [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent] with the identity cover of $X_m^{r+1}$ to conclude that the endpoint square is cartesian. For $r=0$ the vertical maps are identities, so the same conclusion holds. These are the actual naturality squares of the given coherent diagram, since the equivalence of models is natural on diagrams and maps.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, proof paragraph beginning with the pointwise presheaf colimit; expand its structural cartesian squares using Theorem 4.5.3 and the labelled Segal formula

proof.text:
Form the pointwise presheaf colimit $F=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}F_n$ in $P(B_\otimes)$, which exists by [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model], and put $X=F([0])=|X_\bullet|$. For the fixed label $q$ of step 2, the transformation of simplicial spaces $F_\bullet(q)\to X_\bullet^{r+1}$ is cartesian on every arrow. Cartesian geometric descent and finite-product compatibility in [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent] therefore give, for every degree $n$, a natural equivalence over $X_n^{r+1}$,
$$F_n(q)\simeq X_n^{r+1}\times_{X^{r+1}}F(q).$$
The lower comparison $|X_\bullet^{r+1}|\simeq X^{r+1}$ is the finite-product comparison, not a claim that arbitrary pullbacks commute with geometric realization. All maps in the displayed equivalence are induced by the original cocone and endpoint maps.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, pointwise-colimit and cartesian-square paragraphs; HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9(4), applied to small simplicial diagrams

proof.text:
We check that $F$ is Segal. For $r\geq2$ consider the Segal map over $X^{r+1}$,
$$s_q:F(q)\longrightarrow F([1](b_1))\times_X\cdots\times_X F([1](b_r)).$$
Pull it back along $X_0^{r+1}\to X^{r+1}$. Step 3 identifies its source with $F_0(q)$. For each edge factor, the same step with $r=1$ identifies its pullback along the corresponding pair of coordinates $X_0^2\to X^2$ with $F_0([1](b_i))$. Rearranging these finite pullbacks identifies the pulled-back target with $F_0([1](b_1))\times_{X_0}\cdots\times_{X_0}F_0([1](b_r))$. The pulled-back map is exactly the Segal map of $F_0$, hence an equivalence. By [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent], $X_0\to X$ is surjective on $\pi_0$, so $X_0^{r+1}\to X^{r+1}$ is also surjective on $\pi_0$ (choose a lift component independently in each coordinate). Apply its fiberwise comparison criterion to the square with top row $s_q$ and bottom row $\mathrm{id}_{X^{r+1}}$: the comparison is an equivalence on every fiber after that cover, hence $s_q$ is an equivalence. By [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization], this proves $F\in Q_B$.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, paragraph concluding that the pointwise colimit is already a Segal presheaf; make the endpoint-cover and finite-pullback argument explicit

proof.text:
The presheaf $F$ also has local mapping objects. For every degree $n$ and $x,y\in X_n$, take the fiber at $(x,y)$ of the equivalence in step 3 with $q=[1](b)$. As $b$ varies, this gives the natural equivalence of presheaves
$$H_{F_n}(x,y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H_F(\bar x,\bar y),$$
where the arrow is induced by the cocone. Every pair of points of $X$ is connected by a pair of paths to the image of some pair of points of $X_0$, since $X_0^2\to X^2$ is surjective on $\pi_0$. Homotopy fibers at points connected by those paths are equivalent, naturally in the label $b$. Consequently every $H_F(u,v)$ is equivalent to some $H_{F_0}(x,y)$ and is $S$-local: for each arrow $\phi\to\psi$ of $S$, the map $\operatorname{Map}(\psi,H_F(u,v))\to\operatorname{Map}(\phi,H_F(u,v))$ is identified with the corresponding equivalence for $H_{F_0}(x,y)$. The fiberwise characterization in [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model] now implies $F\in Q_B^S$. If $X$ is empty there are no pairs to check, so this argument requires no nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Observation 8.4 and the fiberwise version of Proposition 8.5 provided by the cited corrected model; GH Theorem 5.6.2, mapping-object fiber paragraph

proof.text: Because $Q_B^S$ is a full subcategory of $P(B_\otimes)$ and $F$ lies in it, the pointwise colimit cocone already is colimiting in $Q_B^S$. Indeed the category of cocones of $F_\bullet$ in $Q_B^S$ is the full subcategory of ambient cocones whose apices belong to $Q_B^S$. The ambient initial cocone with apex $F$ belongs to this subcategory and remains initial there: its mapping space to any such cocone is the same contractible mapping space as in the ambient cocone category. This is the definition of a colimiting cocone in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The equivalence of models in [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model] has a coherent inverse. Apply the two functors to every vertex and simplex of a cocone; their inverse homotopies give inverse equivalences of the two cocone categories, so their initial objects correspond. Thus this cocone gives the geometric realization $C$ of $C_\bullet$ in $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$, with its specified cocone.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, assertion that the pointwise colimit is already local; elementary universal-property check for a full subcategory

proof.text: The model identification of object spaces gives $U(C)\simeq F([0])=X=|X_\bullet|$, and the equivalence identifies every cocone map on object spaces with $X_n\to X$. For every $n$ and $x,y\in X_n$, the natural presheaf equivalence of step 5 represents exactly the map $C_n(x,y)\to C(\bar x,\bar y)$, by naturality of [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model]. Both sides are $S$-local presheaves. Since $P^S(B)$ is a full subcategory of $P(B)$, this equivalence is an equivalence in $P^S(B)\simeq\mathcal V$: its inverse and inverse homotopies also lie in that full subcategory. Thus all these maps of mapping objects are equivalences in $\mathcal V$, and [def-coef-complete-algebroid] says exactly that every cocone $C_n\to C$ is fully faithful. Steps 2-5 used only full faithfulness of the structure maps; no essential-surjectivity assumption on those maps was used.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, conclusion from mapping-object fibers; Theorem 4.5.3 and the definition of full faithfulness
